import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import re

# URL for the species profile
url = "https://nas.er.usgs.gov/queries/FactSheet.aspx?SpeciesID=3243"

# Fetch the page content
response = requests.get(url)
html_content = response.text

# Parse the HTML
soup = BeautifulSoup(html_content, 'html.parser')

# Extract the main content
print("Page title:", soup.title.string if soup.title else "No title found")

# Look for tables containing occurrence data
tables = soup.find_all('table')
print(f"Found {len(tables)} tables on the page")

# Look for specific content sections
content_divs = soup.find_all('div', class_='content')
print(f"Found {len(content_divs)} content divs")

# Look for occurrence information
occurrence_section = soup.find('div', id='occurrences') or soup.find('div', {'id': re.compile(r'occurrence', re.I)})
if occurrence_section:
    print("Found occurrence section")
    print(occurrence_section.get_text()[:500])
else:
    print("No occurrence section found")

# Look for any text containing location information
all_text = soup.get_text()
if 'Florida' in all_text:
    print("Florida mentioned in content")
    # Extract text around Florida mentions
    florida_context = []
    for i, line in enumerate(all_text.split('\n')):
        if 'Florida' in line:
            start = max(0, i-2)
            end = min(len(all_text.split('\n')), i+3)
            florida_context.extend(all_text.split('\n')[start:end])
    print("\n".join(florida_context))

# Save the full HTML for inspection
with open('/mnt/data/amphiprion_ocellaris_page.html', 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write(html_content)
print("Full HTML saved to /mnt/data/amphiprion_ocellaris_page.html")

Based on my search results, I have found the complete answer:

1. The fish species from Finding Nemo is Amphiprion ocellaris (ocellaris clownfish/false clownfish)
2. According to the USGS Nonindigenous Aquatic Species database, this species was found as nonnative in only one location before 2020: Fred Howard Park, Pinellas County, Florida in July 2018
3. The zip code for Fred Howard Park in Tarpon Springs, Pinellas County, Florida is 34689

Since there was only one location found, the answer is just the single five-digit zip code: 34689
